page: Microsoft Azure E112iads_v5 is an isolated virtual machine instance belonging to the EIADSv5 server family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 112 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 56 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. The system is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a 3891 GB SSD and supports Premium Storage. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supporting AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, FMA, and SVM virtualization flags, while lacking AVX-512 capabilities.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU testing and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Cryptographic capabilities are also highly competitive, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the top 10%. Memory subsystem performance is strong, as indicated by a top-tier PassMark memory score and top 25% performance in small-block cached read memory bandwidth, though large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the average range. Single-core performance is generally strong to average, with Geekbench single-core scores in the middle 50% and stress-ng single-core performance in the top 25%.

This instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and large-scale multi-threaded processing. PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations both achieved top 25% performance tiers, demonstrating suitability for high-throughput transactional systems. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though it maintains strong performance for small-to-medium LLM prompt processing. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of dedicated AMD EPYC cores combined with substantial local SSD storage and a high vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers a balanced resource profile for enterprise database hosting and software compilation without the premium cost of GPU-accelerated hardware.

It features 112 dedicated vCPUs (56 physical cores) operating at 3.525 GHz, 672.0 GB of RAM, and a 3891 GB local SSD. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 instance delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance and cryptographic execution, alongside strong database and memory subsystem benchmarks. While single-core speeds and large-block uncached memory bandwidth fall into average ranges, its massive multi-threaded capacity and local storage make it highly effective for enterprise databases, multi-threaded decompression, and software compilation.
